bugs.creator: kevinushey
bugs.summary: sync with upstream TRE + apply R patches

comments.text:
## Summary

Updates the bundled TRE from its 2009 base to current upstream, which has absorbed most of R's local patches; pending upstream PRs restore the rest. Also includes fixes for a couple other issues caught along the way: wrong back-reference matches (PR#17259) and multi-gigabyte allocations when compiling short patterns with nested bounds.

## Details

The sources come from the `r-integration` branch of https://github.com/kevinushey/tre, my fork of upstream TRE (https://github.com/laurikari/tre), at commit 512d52fcef. The branch starts from upstream master at commit 71bfcaf0af39 (2026-05-23, still its head) and merges those PRs. R's own changes are confined to three files. `src/extra/tre/R_changes` lists the PRs and the visible changes, mainly in bound parsing (`a{300,}` is now an error). Upstream PRs 131 and 167 supersede the PR#18995 patch.

Reproducible example: attached as `tre-upstream-sync-repro.R`; it fails before the patch and passes after.

Proposed patches, both against r90915:

- `tre-upstream-sync.diff` replaces `src/extra/tre` (no Makefile changes) and adds cases to `tests/reg-fuzz.R`. `make check` passes on macOS, `reg-fuzz.R` also under ASan, and CI passes on Linux and Windows.
- `regex-unwind-leaks.diff` (independent) stops `grep()`, `gsub()`, `regexpr()`, `regexec()` and `strsplit()` leaking the compiled pattern and translation buffers when an error or `options(warn = 2)` unwinds them.

Also submitted as https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/302 and https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/400, where CI results can be seen. Related: PR#17766.

Note that one of the remaining STF milestones has "Re-enable upstream sync from embedded legacy code" also for TRE.  

Now that this is actively maintained again it would be good to look into using
a system TRE by default (if available), and perhaps add a configure option like

  --with-internal-tre 
  --with-internal-TRE

(not sure which one is better) for controlling this.

Patches welcome ...
comments.creator: Kurt.Hornik
kevinushey
comments.text:
It looks like R already has `--with-system-tre` (off by default), which seems like the natural switch (or would you prefer to change that flag?)

The challenge is upstream: I've proposed the fixes R needs there (https://github.com/laurikari/tre/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3Akevinushey, plus #131 and #142 by the upstream maintainers), but none have been merged yet. The only release is still 0.9.0 from 2024, which is what Debian, Fedora and Homebrew ship. Building R against it today would undo fixes R already has; for example, the PR#18995 patterns read past the pattern buffer again under ASan.

In the meantime, the attached patch covers the upstream-sync part of the milestone: the bundled copy becomes upstream master plus those PRs, with R's own changes confined to three files, so later syncs are a straight copy.
